body:
Hi,

Is `sqlite2` correct, as in sqlite version 2.xx?

While unfortunate, I don't think it's supported by sqlalchemy since a long time, so you should pin the sqlalchemy version.

Sadly this is what happens when we accept backports of new features #8804
Leaving open to get @zzzeek opinion on this. We may be able to work around the issue adding a `if len(row) > 4 and ...`.

Hi,

We are using SQLite version 3.32.3.
ok, this definitely seems a regression, since 3.32.3 is very much supported. I'll update the labels.
wow are we doing a "select *" ? why would number of columns change?
the issue seems to be the index_list pragma, apparently the added the 5th column recenrly
sadly the sqlite documentation does not have the old version docs like postrgresql does, so it's a bit hard to understand when that changed

strange. It seems that the output is the same since at least 3.8.9 released in 2015: https://web.archive.org/web/20150428081505/http://www.sqlite.org:80/pragma.html

I may be looking at the wrong place

partial indexes were added in 3.8.0 https://www.sqlite.org/releaselog/3_8_0.html but I don't know if they updated that pragma in that version, it may wery well be so, but the documentation was updated only later

every time I have to do this with sqlite I just get annoyed how people keep calling this project so incredibly well done.  not one mention of anything about this change in their full one page changelog: https://www.sqlite.org/changes.html

> Hi,
> 
> We are using SQLite version 3.32.3.

an install of Python 3.6 on centos7 installs 3.7.17 unless you are doing a custom build.  I can reproduce the problem on centos7:

```py
Python 3.6.8 (default, Nov 16 2020, 16:55:22) 
[GCC 4.8.5 20150623 (Red Hat 4.8.5-44)] on linux
Type "help", "copyright", "credits" or "license" for more information.
>>> import sqlite3
>>> sqlite3.sqlite_version
'3.7.17'
```

ok so the issue is sqlite 3.8 added partial indexes, so previously `index_list` it would have 4 cols, not 5

@yogeshmahajan-1903 can you confirm that you are using sqlite3 `3.32.3`?
@zzzeek we can add a workaround for 1.4 and raise the min supported version in 2? (aka keel like this but update the min supported version to be 3.8.+
